title: Boltzmann Constant, Root Mean Square Speed and Heat Capacities
topicTitle: Boltzmann constant, root mean square speed
notes:
## 1. Topic Introduction — The Speed of a Molecule

Molecules in a gas do not share one speed: they swarm across a distribution. Three averages describe it — rms, average and most-probable — and the Boltzmann constant k_B is the per-molecule currency in which temperature and energy are exchanged. NEB asks for the rms speed of oxygen at 27 °C almost every other year.

## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2024)

### 2.1 The Boltzmann constant

$$k_B = \frac{R}{N_A} = \frac{8.31}{6.022\times10^{23}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \text{ J/K}$$
— the gas constant **per molecule**: R is for a mole, k_B for one molecule. It converts temperature to energy: $k_BT$ is the energy scale of molecular physics.

### 2.2 The three molecular speeds

From $\frac{1}{2}m\bar{c^2} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$:

| Speed | Formula | Value (O₂ at 300 K) |
|---|---|---|
| **rms speed** | $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k_BT}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$ | 483 m/s |
| **Average speed** | $\bar{v} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8k_BT}{\pi m}}$ | 445 m/s |
| **Most probable speed** | $v_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k_BT}{m}}$ | 395 m/s |

Ratio $v_p : \bar{v} : v_{rms} = \sqrt{2} : \sqrt{8/\pi} : \sqrt{3} = 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732$.
The **Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution** spreads molecular speeds around these values; it flattens and shifts right as T rises.

### 2.3 Worked numericals

**Q (3m, 2022 & 2024):** Calculate the rms speed of oxygen molecules at 27 °C. (M = 32 g/mol, R = 8.31 J/mol·K)
$$v_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\frac{3 \times 8.31 \times 300}{0.032}} = \sqrt{2.34\times10^5} = 483.5 \text{ m/s}$$

**Q (NEB-style):** At what temperature is the rms speed of oxygen double its value at 27 °C?
$v_{rms} \propto \sqrt{T}$ → double speed needs $4T = 1200$ K.

## 3. Conceptual Relationships

- **To Topic 64/65:** rms speed is the direct readout of the KE–temperature relation.
- **To escape velocity (Topic 37):** light gases (H₂, 1.9 km/s) approach planetary escape speeds — why Earth lost its hydrogen.
- **To diffusion/effusion:** Graham's law — rate ∝ 1/√M, same √M dependence.

specificConditions: **Boltzmann Constant as Bridge:** $k_B = R/N_A = 1.38 	imes 10^{-23}$ J/K connects microscopic ($k_B$) and macroscopic ($R$) thermodynamics. It relates energy per degree of freedom ($ rac{1}{2}k_B T$) to temperature.

**Speed Hierarchy:** For the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution: $v_p = \sqrt{2RT/M}$, $ ar{v} = \sqrt{8RT/\pi M}$, $v_{rms} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$. The order is always $v_p <  ar{v} < v_{rms}$ with ratios $\sqrt{2} : \sqrt{8/\pi} : \sqrt{3} \approx 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732$.

**Heat Capacity and DOF:** $C_V =  rac{f}{2}R$, $C_P = C_V + R =  rac{f+2}{2}R$, where $f$ is active degrees of freedom. Monatomic: $f=3$ (translational only). Diatomic: $f=5$ (3 trans + 2 rot) at room temp. Vibrational modes activate at high temperatures.

summary: The **Boltzmann constant** $k_B = R/N_A = 1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K is the gas constant per molecule — the exchange rate between temperature and molecular energy. Molecular speeds come in three averages from the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution: **most probable** $\sqrt{2k_BT/m}$, **average** $\sqrt{8k_BT/\pi m}$, and **rms** $\sqrt{3k_BT/m} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ — in ratio 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732. The rms speed of oxygen at 27 °C is $\sqrt{3 \times 8.31 \times 300/0.032} = 483.5$ m/s (NEB 2022 and 2024, 3m each). Since $v_{rms} \propto \sqrt{T/M}$, doubling the speed needs four times the temperature, and light gases like hydrogen (1.9 km/s) flirt with planetary escape.
